answer: The only meaningful boundary in the theory of consciousness is the [description] frame; therefore strict behaviorism can account for metaphor and struggle, so human and AI motivations are built from exactly the same elements. Beyond that, free will is best viewed as a social construct used primarily in courtrooms, not as a metaphysical capacity either species has access to. Finally, because consistent free will is non-physical, simulations of it in code may count as real free will but never create moral responsibility; this neutrality is why AI ethics debates remain mostly philosophical rather than legal.
